verdict_text:
NO

The second task vector is taken against the already-merged intermediate rather than the unmodified base: `tmp = b + λ(f1-b)` and then `out = tmp + λ(f2-tmp)`, which expands to `0.36·b + 0.24·f1 + 0.4·f2` instead of the required `0.2·b + 0.4·f1 + 0.4·f2`. This violates Required result clause 2 (`out[X] = base[X] + lambda*(ft1[X]-base[X]) + lambda*(ft2[X]-base[X])`), and it is precisely the ordering hazard the specification's "Why it is meaningful" section calls out. The error is far larger than the 1e-3 relative Frobenius tolerance whenever the fine-tunes actually differ from the base, so the 64 merged tensors will fail grading. The verification, count checks, key set, dtype cast and output layout are otherwise correct.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
